As a veterinary technician, there has been a lot of discussion in my field about whether this is a good thing or a bad thing. On the one hand, it would give us a better ability to pursue apparent abuse - we are oftentimes hand-tied due to confidentiality, unless we have proof of abuse. On the other hand, it means there may be more disputes concerning custody and right-to-treat animals - proof of ownership may be needed, and people who find an injured animal on the street may not have the legal right to treat it. Obviously none of these issues are decided or probably on the radar at the moment in the mainstream, but this is where both sides of the argument in the veterinary field seem to lay.

I, for one, think this is a great move and hope that cities and states in the US see fit to move this direction as well. It can only bode well for the moral and ethical heart of our civilization to treat all living, feeling beings as deserving of compassion.

Up until just a few decades ago, anesthesia wasn't used on babies because it was thought that their nervous systems weren't well-developed enough to feel real pain. Today, we still don't use anesthetic for tail docking in young puppies for the same reason. We inflict cosmetic procedures on animals to make them suit us, completely disregarding the pain we inflict on them as a result. It's time we did something about that.
Wish I could give you more upvoats. Thank you for a thoughtful comment.

A promising new treatment for multiple sclerosis
A promising new treatment for multiple sclerosis

Although this is a potential avenue for further research, B-cell targeted therapies are proving very effective in clinical practice (for instance, see http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3699597/). As we've progressed in our understanding of MS, we've gone from focusing predominantly on T lymphocytes as the key cell type to mediate inflammatory damage within central nervous system (CNS) lesions, to realizing that B lymphocytes may play a comparably important, if not more significant, role both as precursors of antibody-secreting plasma cells and as antigen-presenting cells (APCs) for the activation of T cells. With greater appreciation of this pathogenic B-cell function in MS, B-cell-directed therapies, and in particular B-cell-depleting monoclonal antibodies targeting the CD20 molecule, have gained recognition as being highly effective therapies. The reason rituximab is not FDA approved for use in MS is because it has been a generic drug since discovering its utility in MS. The cost is very high for drug companies to get FDA approval to market a drug for a specific disease. If a drug is already generic, the drug companies can't make any money off it once it's approved, so they would never waste their money getting it approved for a new disease. If a drug is not approved for a disease by the FDA, then insurance companies won't cover it's cost for patients. Even if it has the best evidence for efficacy against the disease, and expert clinicians in the field have accepted its efficacy, the FDA will not approve it without a multi-million-dollar approval process, and if it's not FDA approved, insurance companies won't pay for it, which means patients can't afford it, and the best treatments are being withheld from the people who would benefit most. I'm working in the field, and consider this to be a crime against humanity.
It is sad indeed. I wonder what the situation outside of the US (and its insurance companies) is like.

Banished
For a few hours this is an interesting city building/city survival experience, but after that flaws with the population and mechanics start to come through that ruin the long-term experience. It also doesn't cater to large-scale city design, so I'm not sure that it really has the replayability found in normal city building games.

 

BIT.TRIP RUNNER
A great musical experience - you control a running character - telling him to jump, slide, etc in time with the rhythm. You have no control over his speed, and if you time your moves properly they act as music notes in the song. Hit an obstacle and you have to start over. Difficult but fun.

 

Shadowgrounds
This game had a great atmosphere - I'm sure it's a little dated at this point, but it still gives a good sci-fi horror vibe that you don't find in too many titles. A lot attempt it, but this one got it right.

 

Shadowgrounds Survivor
Better graphics configuration options than the original game, but the atmosphere isn't as good as the original game, unfortunately.

 

Influx
A marble-type game, with decent puzzles which don't give you an overview - which often means playing them twice. Once to figure out where you need to go, and a second time to properly execute your strategy. This lack of polish prevented me from truly enjoying the game.

 

Bioshock Triple Pack
BioShock 1 is an FPS with a great atmosphere and unique environment, the only thing I really had an issue with were the big daddies - which were frustrating to fight.

Infinite had combat that was very similar to a normal FPS, and again had an interesting world. Additionally you get a brilliant AI companion, although mid-game it does start feeling a bit fetch-questish.

 

Delve Deeper
Too random to be a fun strategic experience, and also lacking online multiplayer. You could play it local multiplayer, but who does that anymore? Since it's very luck based it isn't something I'd enjoy playing against AI either.

 

PixelJunk Eden
An odd little game that feels a bit like being a bug, jumping and swinging around in the tall grass. I'm not really sure what the target demographic is for this game - it wasn't bad but I also didn't love it.

 

PixelJunk Shooter
A little shooter with liquid physics where you fly around rescuing little scientists. It wasn't super exciting, but was a decently polished experience, and for $0.89 it's well worth giving it a shot.

 

Shadow of Mordor
The gameplay in this was solid, with the overall collectables and roaming feeling very much like Assassin's Creed. The combat was pretty easy - somewhat satisfying but would have been better if there was actually a chance of you dieing in a swarm of enemies. Currently you can just dash around and hop over dudes and be nearly invincible unless you mess up. Fun, but not difficult.

My video review is also based on the main game - there have been DLC that may have completed the story, but the main game itself kind of leaves you hanging.

 

Assassin's Creed 4: Black Flag
A lot of the land gameplay is very similar to other Assassin's Creed games, but the sailing in this game is fantastic - and I love all the scenes aboard ships. Those are what really set it apart from similar games and give it a great feel.
